title: Workload Rhythmifier: continuous inference pacing & cache-aware recommendations
creator: Arielle Chen
description: Build a continuous 'Workload Rhythmifier' service that profiles request pacing and cache locality to produce safe batching and cache TTL recommendations. Unlike static heuristics, Rhythmifier will synthesize short-term tempo (ms-level inter-arrival distributions), medium-term seasonality (minute/hour windows), and KV cache hit predictiveness to propose per-route configuration: batch_size, batch_timeout_ms, batch_window_shaping, kv_cache_ttl_ms and a smoothing_factor for continuous knob application. The service will provide dry-run simulation, shadow apply, canary rollout, automated rollback triggers tied to latency SLO regressions and per-token cost deltas.
acceptance_criteria: Service ingests 72h of route-level telemetry and produces per-route recommended knobs with rationale (tempo histogram, burst_index, cache_hit_pred)
Dry-run simulator can replay a day's traffic and predict delta in median latency, p95, and aggregate token cost for recommended knobs
Canary rollout automation can apply recommendations to 5% traffic, monitor SLO/latency/cost signals, and auto-rollback on configured thresholds
UI endpoint in Console shows recommendation history, confidence score, and simulation outputs; audit log retained for 90 days
Integration tests validate no increase >5% in SLO p95 in staging under mixed workloads when recommendation is applied

2026-02-27: Decided to couple cache TTL recommendations with batch_timeout_ms; short TTLs + long batch timeouts cause poor KV reuse. Design doc updated with coupling heuristics (see Confluence link).

implementation_notes: Profiling pipeline: ingest aggregated route telemetry (1m granularity) and a fast sample of raw IATs for bursts. Store snapshots in time-series DB with TTL=30d.

Heuristics: compute burst_index = P(IAT < 50ms) / median(IAT). Recommend batch_size as floor( target_latency_budget / expected_batch_latency ), where expected_batch_latency uses measured kernel latency models.
Cache model: small ensemble (lightweight decision tree + logistic regressor) predicts marginal benefit of increasing kv_cache_ttl for a route given request entropy and model prefix reuse rates.
Continuous apply: recommendations generated every 6 hours; smoothing_factor (0.0-1.0) throttles knob movement to avoid oscillation. Default smoothing=0.25 for production-tier routes.
Safe-apply plumbing: feature-flag controlled canary API, shadow apply mode (no mutate) for dry telemetry, and audit events emitted to console operations timeline.
Rollback triggers: p95_exceedance, error_rate_rise, token_cost_worsen (unexpected increase). All thresholds configurable per-customer-tier.
Observability: add comparison traces (baseline vs suggested) + cost delta projection in Console. Log advice rationale as short human-readable bullet points.
Access controls: only Ops and Platform SRE roles can approve auto-apply for enterprise customers. Record approver in audit log.
risks: Oscillation risk if smoothing_factor too low and multiple routes receive conflicting knob changes simultaneously
Incorrect cache TTL recommendations may increase cold-starts, raising p99 latency for rarely-invoked routes
Model drift in cache benefit predictor — requires periodic retrain and can lead to misleading confidence scores
Customer trust: automated changes could be undesirable for regulated workloads; must support opt-out and manual review
qa_plan: Unit tests for heuristics and simulator deterministic outputs
Integration test: replay 72h production trace in staging and assert p95 and error_rate within thresholds before apply
Chaos tests: inject sudden burst patterns and validate canary rollback triggers
A/B canary: 5% traffic compare against control for 24h across 10 representative routes
oncall_runbook: If canary auto-rollback triggers: notify #infra-cost-ops, run diagnose script /ops/rhythmifier/check_canary.sh, revert to last-known-good knobs, and open incident if >3 routes affected
If simulator predictions diverge >20% from observed cost after apply: pause automation, tag model for retrain, and notify ML-owner
Manual rollback: use Console -> Operations -> Rollouts -> select Rhythmifier rollout -> rollback -> confirm audit entry
